definition_zh: 捐赠；捐款；捐赠物；血液或器官捐献
definition_en: the act of giving money, goods, blood or an organ to help others, or the thing given
core_image: 一只透明的募捐箱，箱底铺满硬币
scene: 医院大厅摆着一只透明的募捐箱，箱底已经铺了一层硬币。 The charity received a large donation from a local factory.
sceneCN: 这里 donation 是「捐款、捐赠物」（第 2 个义项：捐出的钱或物）；句意是这家慈善机构收到了本地一家工厂的一大笔捐款。

pos.zh: 名词：捐赠；捐款；捐赠物；血液或器官捐献

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「捐赠；捐献」
由拉丁词干加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「捐赠者；捐献者」
由拉丁词干加后缀构成，义为「捐赠的；捐赠物」（较少用）

senses.title: The act of giving
senses.definition: the act of giving money or goods to a charity, a cause or a person in need
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或物捐给慈善机构、某项事业或需要帮助的人的行为
senses.example: The donation of the old library building saved it from demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 旧图书馆建筑的捐赠使它免于被拆除。
senses.why: Latin donare meant to give, and donatio named the giving itself before it named the object given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 donare 意为「给」，donatio 先指给予这一行为，后来才指所给之物。

senses.title: Something given
senses.definition: money or goods that are given in this way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式捐出的钱或物品
senses.example: A pile of donations filled the back of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 一车捐赠物堆满了卡车后厢。
senses.why: The act leaves a result behind, and that result becomes the countable thing we call a donation.
senses.whyCN: 行为会留下结果，这个结果就成了可以数的「一笔捐赠、一件捐赠物」。

senses.title: Blood or organ donation
senses.definition: the giving of blood, tissue or an organ for medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为医疗用途捐出血液、组织或器官
senses.example: Regular blood donation helps hospitals keep enough supply.
senses.exampleCN: 定期献血帮助医院维持足够的库存。
senses.why: The same generous giving now applies to the body itself, where the gift can save a life directly.
senses.whyCN: 同样慷慨的给予如今落到身体本身，这份礼物能直接救一条命。

intro.en: Donation comes from Latin donatio, a giving, built on donum, gift, and donare, to give.
intro.cn: donation 来自拉丁语 donatio（给予），其根为 donum（礼物）与 donare（给）。

items.en: The root behind donum is generally reconstructed as a word for giving; its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: donum 背后的词根一般重构为表示「给」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Donum meant a gift, something handed over without payment.
items.cn: donum 指礼物，即无偿交出的东西。

items.en: Donare meant to give, present or grant.
items.cn: donare 意为「给、赠予、授予」。

items.en: Donatio named the act of giving and also the gift itself in legal language.
items.cn: donatio 既指给予的行为，在法律用语里也指赠与之物。

items.en: Old French donation carried the word into English with its charitable tone.
items.cn: 古法语 donation 把这个词带入英语，同时带来慈善色彩。

items.en: Modern medicine added blood and organ donation to the older sense of giving money.
items.cn: 现代医学在「捐钱」这一旧义之外，又加上献血与器官捐献。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin giving root; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of contribution.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「给」的词根；近义组收的是其他形式的贡献。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give money, goods or blood to a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捐赠、捐献」，与 donation 同根。

entries.definition: A person or organisation that gives, especially blood or an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捐赠者、捐献者」，尤指献血或捐器官的人。

entries.definition: A rare adjective or noun for something given as a gift.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「捐赠的；捐赠物」，较少使用。

entries.definition: Money or help given toward a shared purpose; broader and less emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献、捐款」，指为共同目标给出的钱或帮助，范围更广。

entries.definition: Something given to a person, often for pleasure rather than charity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「礼物」，常出于心意而非慈善。

entries.definition: Money given by an institution for a specific purpose, usually after an application.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拨款、补助金」，通常由机构在申请后给出。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real donum family and the three kinds of giving it now covers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 donum 词族，以及它今天覆盖的三种给予。

normal.en: Donum is a gift; donare is to give; donatio is the giving.
normal.cn: donum 是礼物，donare 是给，donatio 是给予这件事。

normal.en: Donate, donor and donation all keep the same giving stem.
normal.cn: donate、donor 与 donation 都保留同一个「给」的词干。

normal.en: A donation can be a sum of money or the act of writing the cheque.
normal.cn: donation 既可以是那笔钱，也可以是写支票这个行为。

normal.en: Blood donation is the same gift applied to the body.
normal.cn: 献血是把同一份礼物用在身体上。

normal.en: A donor is the person on the giving side of the noun.
normal.cn: donor 就是这件事里站在给予一方的人。

abstract.en: Picture a clear box slowly filling with coins at a hospital door.
abstract.cn: 想象医院门口一只透明箱子，硬币一点点堆起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing a folded note across a counter and letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把折好的纸币递过柜台，然后松开。

abstract.en: Picture one arm offered while another person waits for help.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂伸出来，另一个人在等着这份帮助。

examples.en: The school received a donation of thirty new desks.
examples.cn: 学校收到捐赠的三十张新课桌。

examples.en: She made a small monthly donation to the animal shelter.
examples.cn: 她每月向动物收容所捐一小笔钱。

examples.en: The clinic urgently needs blood donations of the rarest type.
examples.cn: 这家诊所急需最稀有血型的献血。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兜内」——把兜里的钱拿出来放进募捐箱，就是一份 donation。

root: 源自拉丁语 donatio（给予），由 donare（给）加名词后缀 -tio 构成，其根为 donum（礼物）。本义是「无偿给予」这一行为，后来既指捐出的钱物，也扩展到献血与器官捐献。

sensesIntro.en: One giving root covers the act, the thing given, and the gift of blood or an organ.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「给」的词根，覆盖给予的行为、所给之物，以及血液或器官这份礼物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear collection box with coins settled at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只透明募捐箱，硬币沉在箱底。

branches.en: THE ACT: the first sense is the giving itself, before any object is counted.
branches.cn: 行为线：第一个义项是给予本身，尚未去数具体东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the second sense is what the act leaves behind in the box.
branches.cn: 实物线：第二个义项是行为留在箱子里的东西。

branches.en: THE BODY: the third sense gives blood or an organ instead of money.
branches.cn: 身体线：第三个义项给的不是钱，而是血或器官。

branches.en: The act and the object share one noun because a gift exists only through being given.
branches.cn: 行为与实物共用一个名词，因为礼物正是通过被给出才存在。

branches.en: Money and blood are both things handed over so that someone else can live better.
branches.cn: 钱与血都是交出去、好让别人的日子好过一些的东西。

intro.en: Donation is a Latin action noun in -tio built on donare, to give, and donum, gift.
intro.cn: donation 是拉丁语以 -tio 结尾的动作名词，建立在 donare（给）与 donum（礼物）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin donum, donare and donatio are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 donum、donare 与 donatio 均有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是礼物本身。

items.example: The verb names the act of giving.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指给予的动作。

items.example: The Latin noun became English donation.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词变成了英语 donation。

items.example: The donor wished to remain unnamed.
items.exampleCN: 这位捐赠者希望不留名。

definition_zh: 边界；前沿；边疆
definition_en: a border between places, or the leading edge of knowledge
core_image: 荒野尽头立着一块旧木界碑
scene: 这条河曾是两个国家的边界。 The river was once the frontier between two countries.
sceneCN: 这里 frontier 是「边界」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这条河曾是两个国家的边界。

derivatives.zh: 前面
边疆居民

senses.title: A border
senses.definition: the line or land between two countries
senses.definitionCN: 两个国家之间的界线或地带
senses.example: The river was once the frontier between two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河曾是两个国家的边界。
senses.why: This is the political and geographic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是政治与地理义项。

senses.title: The edge of settlement
senses.definition: the outer edge of settled land
senses.definitionCN: 已开发土地的外缘
senses.example: They built a fort on the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在边疆建了一座堡垒。
senses.why: A national border is also the edge of home.
senses.whyCN: 国界也是家园的边缘。

senses.title: The leading edge
senses.definition: the most advanced part of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 某学科最先进的部分
senses.example: She works at the frontier of medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她在医学前沿工作。
senses.why: Knowledge also has land not yet settled.
senses.whyCN: 知识也有尚未开垦的土地。

intro.en: Frontier comes from the word front.
intro.cn: frontier 来自 front 这个词。

items.en: Frons meant forehead.
items.cn: frons 意为额头。

items.en: Frontiere meant the front of an army.
items.cn: frontiere 意为军队的前线。

items.en: It named the edge of a country.
items.cn: 它用来指国家的边缘。

items.en: It described the edge of settlement.
items.cn: 它描述定居点的边缘。

items.en: It now also means a limit of knowledge.
items.cn: 如今它也指知识的极限。

normalIntro.en: A frontier is the front edge of a known world.
normalIntro.cn: frontier 是已知世界的前沿边缘。

normal.en: The river was once the frontier between two countries.
normal.cn: 这条河曾是两个国家的边界。

normal.en: They built a fort on the frontier.

normal.en: She works at the frontier of medicine.

normal.en: A frontier town grew beside the road.

normal.en: Space is often called the final frontier.

abstract.en: A frontier is a line that invites questions.

abstract.en: Beyond the known there is always more land.
abstract.cn: 已知之外总有更多土地。

abstract.en: The frontier of today becomes the home of tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 今日的前沿会成为明日的家园。

examples.en: The river was once the frontier between two countries.

dict_mnemonic.text: front（前面）+ -ier = frontier，字面就是「最前面的那一条」；由国界引申为「边疆」，再引申为科学「前沿」。

sensesIntro.en: Frontier means a border, the edge of settlement, or the leading edge of knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: frontier 意为边界、边疆或前沿。

core.en: The outermost line of a known area.

branches.en: A river divides two countries.

branches.en: A fort guards the edge of settlement.

branches.en: A doctor explores unknown medicine.

definition_zh: 拼图；谜题；难题；使困惑；苦思
definition_en: a game or problem that tests thought; something difficult to understand; to make someone confused; to think hard about something
core_image: 散落一桌的小块，拼到最后才露出完整图案
scene: 桌上摊着一张画满格子的纸，旁边散着几百块小纸板，孩子已经坐了半个下午。 He could not finish the puzzle until he saw the picture on the box.
sceneCN: 这里 puzzle 是「拼图」（第 1 个义项：需要拼合图形的智力玩具）；句意为直到看见盒子上的图，他才把拼图拼完。画面里可留意：格子纸、小纸板、盒子。

derivatives.zh: puzzle 加名词后缀 -ment，指被难住时的困惑状态
puzzle 加表人或表物后缀 -er，指难题，也指爱解谜的人
puzzle 与 box 复合，指要按机关才能打开的盒子

senses.title: A game made of pieces that fit together
senses.definition: a game or toy in which many small pieces must be fitted together to form a picture or a shape
senses.definitionCN: 把许多小块拼合起来、组成图案或形状的游戏或玩具
senses.example: The children spread the puzzle over the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把拼图摊满了整张桌子。
senses.why: The word first named a confusing problem, then was applied to the cut-up picture because solving one feels like rebuilding a broken whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指令人困惑的难题，后来用在被切成碎块的图画上，因为拼合它就像把一个破碎的整体重新装回去。

senses.title: Something difficult to understand
senses.definition: a question, situation or person that is hard to understand or explain
senses.definitionCN: 难以理解或解释的问题、局面或人
senses.example: How the thief entered the locked room remains a puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 窃贼如何进入那间锁着的屋子仍是个谜。
senses.why: From the start the word named what stops the mind, so any event with a missing piece is called by the name of the game.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一开始就指「卡住思路的东西」，因此任何缺了一块的事，都能用这项游戏的名字来称呼。

senses.title: To confuse someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel confused because they cannot understand something
senses.definitionCN: 使某人因为弄不明白而感到困惑
senses.example: The letter puzzled her for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她困惑了很久。
senses.why: If a problem is a puzzle, then meeting it is being caught inside it, so the noun turned into a verb of bafflement.
senses.whyCN: 既然难题本身是 puzzle，遇上它就像被它困在里面，于是名词转成了表示「使人为难」的动词。

senses.title: To think hard about something
senses.definition: to think long and carefully about something you cannot understand or solve
senses.definitionCN: 对无法理解或解决的事长时间仔细思考
senses.example: He puzzled over the figures until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他对着那些数字苦思到半夜。
senses.why: The mind keeps returning to a piece it cannot place, and that repeated turning is the second life of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 心思会一次次回到那块放不下的拼图上，这种反复琢磨正是这个动词的第二重生命。

intro.en: Puzzle appears in English in the late sixteenth century, and its origin is uncertain; it may be a frequentative of pose in an older sense of perplexing someone, but no Latin cognate can be traced with confidence.
intro.cn: puzzle 在十六世纪后期出现在英语中，来源不确定；它可能是 pose 旧义「把人问住」的反复形式，但没有可确证的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as pusle, meaning to bewilder or confuse, with no earlier French or Latin form securely attached to it.
items.cn: 这个动词最早记作 pusle，意为使人迷惑，此前并没有可确证的法语或拉丁语形式与它相连。

items.en: Several explanations have been offered and none is accepted as certain, so dictionaries usually mark the origin as unknown.
items.cn: 人们提出过几种解释，但没有一种被公认，所以词典通常把来源标为不明。

items.en: One common suggestion is that the word is a frequentative of pose in the old sense to put someone to a standstill; this is generally described as possible rather than proved.
items.cn: 一种常见的说法是，它是 pose 旧义「使人僵住、问住」的反复形式；一般认为这只是可能，而非已证。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the noun named a bewildering question, and by the nineteenth century it was applied to the jigsaw picture cut into pieces.
items.cn: 十七世纪名词 puzzle 指令人困惑的问题，到十九世纪又被用在切成碎块的拼图上。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for the toy, the enigma and the act of thinking hard, and keeps puzzling as an adjective for what confuses.
items.cn: 现代英语用 puzzle 指玩具、谜团与苦思的动作，并用 puzzling 作形容词表示令人困惑的。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem and two words that merely rhyme; the near-meaning group collects other names for what is hard to explain.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收其他表示「难以解释之物」的词。

entries.definition: Hard to understand or explain.
The feeling of being confused by something.
The nose and mouth of an animal, or a guard over them; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的口鼻部，或罩在上面的套子；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To rub against something gently with the nose; only the sound is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用鼻子轻轻蹭某物；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A question or statement that needs clever thought to answer.
entries.definitionCN: 需要巧思才能回答的问题或说法。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is mysterious and hard to read.
Something that cannot be explained or is kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 无法解释或被保密的事。

entries.definition: A network of paths designed to be hard to escape.
entries.definitionCN: 设计得难以走出的路径网。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a verb for confusing the mind, and the toy borrowed the name because it does the same thing more gently.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一个使人脑子打结的动词，玩具借用了这个名字，只因它更温和地做着同一件事。

normal.en: The verb first meant to bewilder, and the toy took the name because a cut picture bewilders until the last piece fits.
normal.cn: 这个动词最早表示使人迷惑，玩具之所以得名，是因为在最后一块拼上之前，碎图同样让人摸不着头绪。

normal.en: Puzzlement adds -ment and names the feeling, while puzzler adds -er and names the hard question itself.
normal.cn: puzzlement 加 -ment 指那种感受，puzzler 加 -er 则指难题本身。

normal.en: Puzzling drops the final e before -ing and keeps the sense of something that confuses.
normal.cn: puzzling 在加 -ing 前去掉词尾的 e，保留「令人困惑」之意。

normal.en: Puzzle over is the pattern for thinking hard: the preposition points at the thing that will not fit.
normal.cn: puzzle over 是苦思的固定搭配：介词指向那块怎么也放不进去的东西。

normal.en: Jigsaw puzzle is a compound from the saw that once cut the picture, though few speakers now think of the tool.
normal.cn: jigsaw puzzle 是由从前切割图画的锯子构成的复合词，如今很少有人再想到那件工具。

abstract.en: A puzzle promises that every scattered piece has one place and only one.
abstract.cn: 拼图许下的承诺是：每一块散落的碎片都有一个、且只有一个位置。

abstract.en: The pleasure lies not in the picture but in the second when two pieces refuse to fit and then do.

sceneCN: 这里 offend 是「冒犯、使不快」（第 1 个义项：使别人感到被冒犯）；句意是他拿她家乡开的玩笑，让聚会上好几位客人不快。画面里是一群围坐的人，笑声突然停住。

senses.title: To make someone feel upset or insulted
senses.definition: to say or do something that hurts someone's feelings or insults them
senses.definitionCN: 说出或做出伤害别人感情、使人受辱的话或事
senses.example: His joke offended several guests at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个玩笑得罪了聚会上的好几位客人。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to strike against, and a remark can strike a person just as a blow can.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「撞上」，而一句话也能像一拳那样撞到人身上。

senses.title: To commit a crime or a wrong
senses.definition: to commit a crime or do something morally wrong
senses.definitionCN: 犯下罪行，或做出道德上错误的事
senses.example: He offended repeatedly before he was finally caught.
senses.exampleCN: 他屡次作案，最终才被抓。
senses.why: Offendere also meant to stumble or to transgress, and English kept that sense for breaking a law or a moral code.
senses.whyCN: offendere 也有「失足、越界」的意思，英语保留了这层，用来指触犯法律或道德规范。

senses.title: To break a rule or principle
senses.definition: to go against a rule, a principle or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背某条规则、原则或标准
senses.example: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策违反了同工同酬的原则。
senses.why: With against, the verb points the blow at an abstract standard rather than a person, so the insult turns into a violation.
senses.whyCN: 接上 against 时，这一击指向的不再是人，而是一条抽象标准，于是「冒犯」转为「违反」。

senses.title: To be unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: to be offensive to the eye, the ear or the nose
senses.definitionCN: 使眼睛、耳朵或鼻子感到不适
senses.example: The bright green paint offends the eye in that quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 在那间素净的屋子里，那面亮绿色的墙看着很扎眼。
senses.why: Since a blow can land on the body, the same verb can describe what jars the senses, which is the last step from people to eyes and noses.
senses.whyCN: 既然一击能落在人身上，同一个动词也能形容刺到感官的东西，这就是从人走到眼睛与鼻子的最后一步。

intro.en: Offend is a Latin verb for striking against that came through French, and its sense moved from stumbling and sinning to hurting feelings.
intro.cn: offend 是拉丁语中表示「撞上去」的动词，经法语进入英语，词义从失足、犯罪一路走到伤害感情。

items.en: Offendere joined ob-, meaning against, with fendere, meaning to strike, so its first picture was a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: offendere 把表示「对着」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 合在一起，最初的画面是朝着某物打出一击。

items.en: In Latin the verb also meant to stumble against an obstacle and to transgress, which prepared the later moral senses.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中，这个动词还表示撞上障碍、失足，以及越界，这为后来的道德义埋下了伏笔。

items.en: Old French offendre meant to wrong or to sin, and it supplied English with the verb in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 offendre 意为冒犯或犯罪，中世纪时把这个动词送进了英语。

items.en: Middle English offenden first meant to sin or to transgress, and only later came to mean to displease a person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offenden 最初指犯罪、越界，后来才引申为使人不快。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the legal sense of breaking a rule and the everyday sense of hurting someone's feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「违反规则」的法律义与「伤害感情」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and adjectives of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for hurting feelings and breaking rules.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族的名词与形容词；近义组收表示伤人感情与违反规则的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of striking that turned into a family of nouns and adjectives about wrongdoing and wounded feelings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示打击的动词，后来长成一族指过错与伤人感情的名词与形容词。

normal.en: Ob- plus fendere gives a blow aimed at someone, and that is the physical core of offend.
normal.cn: ob- 加 fendere 就是朝人打出的一击，这就是 offend 的身体性内核。

normal.en: Offend against is the pattern for breaking a law or a principle, not for hurting a person.
normal.cn: offend against 是违反法律或原则的固定搭配，而不是指伤害某个人。

normal.en: Offender adds -er to the verb: the person who lands the blow or commits the crime.
normal.cn: offender 在动词后加 -er，就是打出这一击、犯下罪行的那个人。

normal.en: Be offended by marks the receiver of the blow, the person whose feelings were hurt.
normal.cn: be offended by 标出的是承受一击的一方，也就是感情受伤的人。

normal.en: Offend the eye shows that the verb can strike senses as well as feelings.
normal.cn: offend the eye 说明这个动词不只打击感情，也能打击感官。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone thrown in conversation: it leaves no mark on the skin, but offend names the bruise underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象谈话中扔出的一颗小石子：皮肤上没有痕迹，而 offend 就是底下那块淤青的名字。

abstract.en: A step over a rule touches the law first and someone's feelings second, and one verb covers both.
abstract.cn: 越过规则的那一步，先触到法律，再触到别人的感受，同一个动词把两者都收下了。

abstract.en: Offence is often unintended, yet it still lands on the other person; that gap is what the word keeps alive.
abstract.cn: 冒犯常常不是本意，却仍然落在对方身上；这道落差正是这个词一直保留的东西。

examples.en: His joke offended several guests at the party.

examples.en: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.

examples.en: Loud colours offend the eye in such a quiet room.
examples.cn: 在这样素净的房间里，刺眼的颜色看着很不舒服。

definition_zh: 因此；所以；结果
definition_en: as a result of what has just been said

scene: 雨下了一整夜，清晨的街道空了一半。 The road flooded and consequently the school closed.

senses.title: As a result
senses.definition: as a result of something just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 由于刚提到的事而产生结果
senses.example: He missed the train and consequently arrived late.
senses.exampleCN: 他错过了火车，因此到得很晚。
senses.why: One fact ends, and the next one starts from its edge.
senses.whyCN: 一件事实结束，下一件就从它的边缘开始。

senses.title: In a logical order
senses.definition: in a way that follows logically from the facts

senses.example: The figures were wrong and consequently the report was useless.
senses.exampleCN: 数字错了，所以这份报告毫无用处。
senses.why: A chain of reasoning needs a word to mark where the chain lands.
senses.whyCN: 一条推理链需要一个词，标出链条落在哪里。

senses.title: Following in time
senses.definition: happening next in time or order, an older and rarer sense

senses.why: Before it marked reasons, the word simply marked the next step.

items.en: English consequent entered as an adjective of result.

sceneCN: 这里 mid 是「悬在半空、处在中间位置」的意思（第 2 个义项：空间或位置的中间）；句意为攀爬者在半空中停了一下，检查绳索再继续往上。画面里可抓住的物件：岩壁、绳索、路中央的小标牌。

senses.title: Halfway through a period of time
senses.definition: in the middle part of a month, year, decade or other stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个月、某一年、某个十年等一段时间的中间部分
senses.example: The store is busiest in mid-December.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在十二月中旬最忙。
senses.why: The oldest form of the word simply meant middle, so the first place it settled was time: a point that cuts a long stretch into two halves, as in mid-December and the mid-1990s.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的形式本义就是「中间」，所以它最先固定下来的用法是时间：一个把整段时间分成两半的位置，于是有 mid-December 与 the mid-1990s 这样的说法。

senses.title: The middle of a place or space
senses.definition: located in the central part of a space, especially while in the air or over water
senses.definitionCN: 处在某个空间的中央部分，尤指悬在空中或水面之上
senses.example: The bird hovered in mid-air above the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟在湖面上方的半空中悬停。
senses.why: Because mid marks a point between two ends, it naturally describes a body held between ground and sky, or between two shores; joining it to air keeps the short word usable on its own.
senses.whyCN: 因为 mid 标记的是两端之间的一个位置，所以它顺理成章地用来形容悬在地面与天空之间、或两岸之间的物体；与 air 连用，则让这个短词能够独立出现。

senses.title: Partway through an action or process
senses.definition: while an action or event is already under way and has not yet finished
senses.definitionCN: 在一个动作或事件已经开始、尚未结束的时候
senses.example: She stood up in mid-sentence and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她话说到一半就站起来离开了房间。
senses.why: An action also has a beginning and an end, so the same midpoint applies to speech, flight or a match; mid-sentence and mid-flight are direct extensions of the time sense.
senses.whyCN: 动作同样有开头和结尾，同一个「中间点」便顺延到说话、飞行或比赛之中；mid-sentence 与 mid-flight 都是时间义的直接延伸。

senses.title: In the middle of a range or scale
senses.definition: of a size, price or level, positioned between the low and high ends
senses.definitionCN: 指尺寸、价格或水平处在低端与高端之间
senses.example: They chose a mid-range phone rather than the most expensive one.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选了一部中档手机，而不是最贵的那款。
senses.why: A scale is laid out like a line with two ends, so mid can name the band in between; that is why shops and ratings say mid-range and mid-level instead of coining another adjective.
senses.whyCN: 等级序列像一条有两个端点的线，mid 因而能指中间那一档；商店与评级说 mid-range、mid-level 而不另造形容词，正是这个道理。

senses.title: Forming compounds for the middle part
senses.titleCN: 构成复合词指某物的中部
senses.definition: used as the first element of compounds that name the central part of a place, body or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作复合词的第一部分，用来指某个地点、身体部位或组织的中部
senses.example: The midfielder ran back to help the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 那名中场球员跑回来协助防守。
senses.why: English often presses a short adjective into service as a prefix; mid joined field, week and section to name the central zone without inventing a new root for each one.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个短形容词直接拿来当前缀；mid 与 field、week、section 组合，指出中间那块区域，而不必为每个概念另造词根。

intro.en: Mid is one of the oldest words in English; it descends from a reconstructed root for middle and has a genuine Latin cousin in medius.
intro.cn: mid 是英语中最古老的词之一，源自一个表示「中间」的重构词根，并在拉丁语里有真正的同族词 medius。

items.en: The reconstructed root *medhyo- meant middle, and Latin medius also grew from it; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by linguists, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 重构词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，拉丁语 medius 也出自它；星号表示这是语言学家重建的形式，并非有记录的原词。

items.en: The Germanic branch kept the root as *midjaz, which entered Old English with the same meaning.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族把这词根保留为 *midjaz，带着相同的「中间」义进入古英语。

items.en: Old English midd worked as both adjective and noun, and it already formed compounds such as middæg, the middle of the day.
items.cn: 古英语的 midd 可作形容词和名词，并且已经构成 middæg 这类复合词，指一天的中段。

items.en: Middle English shortened the adjective to mid and placed it chiefly before another word, as in midwinter and midnight.
items.cn: 中古英语把形容词缩为 mid，主要把它放在另一个词前面使用，如 midwinter 与 midnight。

items.en: Modern English keeps mid almost entirely in compounds and hyphenated phrases such as mid-air, mid-July and mid-range.
items.cn: 现代英语几乎只在复合词和带连字符的短语里保留 mid，如 mid-air、mid-July 与 mid-range。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same middle root; the near-meaning group collects words for the central point or position.

normalIntro.en: Mid is the short form of an old English word for middle, and the family around it keeps pointing at the place where two halves meet.
normalIntro.cn: mid 是古英语中表示「中间」的词的短形式，围绕它的一族词始终指向两半相接的地方。

normal.en: Mid is the shortened form of an Old English word for middle, so its own meaning needs no separate explanation.
normal.cn: mid 是古英语「中间」一词的缩写形式，它本身的含义无需另作解释。

normal.en: The word prefers company: mid-July, mid-air and mid-range all place it before the thing that is being halved.
normal.cn: 这个词偏好结伴出现：mid-July、mid-air 与 mid-range 都把它放在被分成两半的事物前面。

normal.en: Latin medius is a true cousin, linking mid to words such as median and intermediate.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 是它真正的同族词，把 mid 与 median、intermediate 一类词连在一起。

normal.en: Mid keeps its hyphen when the compound is new or a number follows, as in mid-1990s and mid-sentence.
normal.cn: 当复合词较新或后面接数字时，mid 保留连字符，如 mid-1990s 与 mid-sentence。

normal.en: Compare midday and midnight: the same mid points at noon on one side and at the darkest hour on the other.
normal.cn: 对比 midday 与 midnight：同一个 mid 一边指向正午，一边指向夜里最深的时刻。

abstract.en: Picture a rope tied at its exact centre; everything named with mid hangs from that knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子在正中央打了个结，凡是用 mid 命名的东西都挂在这个结上。

abstract.en: Mid is a hinge word: it never points at an end, only at the place where two halves meet.
abstract.cn: mid 是个铰链式的词：它从不指向端点，只指向两半相接的地方。

abstract.en: A stadium full of people, a flight over the sea, a decade half spent: one small word holds all these middles.
abstract.cn: 坐满人的体育场、飞越海面的航班、过了一半的十年：一个小词装下了所有这些「中间」。

examples.en: The store is busiest in mid-December.
examples.cn: 这家店在十二月中旬最忙。

examples.en: The bird hovered in mid-air above the lake.
examples.cn: 那只鸟在湖面上方的半空中悬停。

examples.en: They chose a mid-range phone.
examples.cn: 他们选了一部中档手机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」——位置卡在正当中的那一点，密得两边一样远；记住 mid 是中间。

root: 古英语 midd（中间）来自原始日耳曼语 *midjaz，更早可追到重构词根 *medhyo-；拉丁语 medius（中间的）是同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core idea is the point between two ends; the senses apply it to time, space, an action in progress, a scale, and compounds naming a middle part.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两端之间的那个点；各义项依次把它用到时间、空间、进行中的动作、等级序列，以及指中部地带的复合词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tied at its exact centre, both ends running away in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绳子在正中央打了结，两端朝相反方向延伸出去。

branches.en: a calendar page folded at the centre of July
branches.cn: 日历翻到七月正中那一页

branches.en: a body hanging between sky and water
branches.cn: 悬在天空与水面之间的身体

branches.en: a sentence cut off before its last word
branches.cn: 话没说完就被截断的一句

branches.en: a row of phones with the middle price tag picked out
branches.cn: 一排手机里被挑出的中间价签

branches.en: a player standing between defence and attack
branches.cn: 站在防守与进攻之间的球员

intro.cn: mid 只在较早的英语里独立作形容词；今天它主要作为构词成分，而拉丁同族词 medius 解释了更广的「中间」词族。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 预防措施；防备；防范；安全防护安排
definition_en: something done in advance to stop trouble from happening, and the care taken before a risk arrives
core_image: 出门前那双手把门窗与煤气阀逐一检查一遍
scene: 台风消息传来，店主把窗板一块块钉上，又把沙袋堆在门缝前。 As a precaution, the shopkeeper boarded up the windows before the storm arrived.
sceneCN: 这里是「预防措施、防备」（第 1 个义项：事先采取的防范做法）；句意为台风到来前，店主把窗户钉上作为防备。图中可辨识物件：窗板、沙袋、店门。

pos.zh: 预防措施；防备；防范；安全防护安排

derivatives.zh: 由 precaution 加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，义为「预防性的；防备的」
precautionary 加 -ly 构成，义为「以预防的方式」

senses.title: A step taken in advance to prevent harm
senses.definition: an action done before a risk arrives, so that the harm it could cause is avoided or reduced
senses.definitionCN: 在风险到来之前就做好的动作，用来避免或减轻它可能造成的伤害
senses.example: Take precautions against theft when you travel.
senses.exampleCN: 出门旅行时要采取防盗措施。
senses.why: The word names a guarding that happens before the danger, so the most common sense is the concrete thing a person does ahead of time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指的是在危险之前完成的「看守」，所以最常见的义项就是人提前做的那件具体的事。

senses.title: Care taken beforehand
senses.definition: the habit or act of being careful in advance, rather than one single measure
senses.definitionCN: 提前保持小心的习惯或做法，而不是某一项具体措施
senses.example: He moved the papers with great precaution, as if they might tear.
senses.exampleCN: 他非常小心地搬动那些文件，仿佛它们随时会破。
senses.why: Strip away the countable measure and what remains is the quality behind it: a watchfulness that starts before anything has gone wrong.
senses.whyCN: 把可数的具体措施抽掉，剩下的是它背后的性质：在事情出错之前就已经开始的警觉。

senses.title: Official safety arrangements
senses.definition: the set of rules and arrangements an institution keeps in place for one particular kind of danger
senses.definitionCN: 机构为某一类危险而长期设置的一整套规定与安排
senses.example: The hotel's fire precautions were inspected last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的消防安排上个月接受了检查。
senses.why: Because measures against one kind of danger are planned together, the plural came to name an organised set rather than separate acts.
senses.whyCN: 针对同一类危险的措施通常是配套规划的，于是复数形式便用来指一套有组织的安排，而不是零散的动作。

intro.en: Precaution is a Latin compound meaning a guarding done before the event, which French passed on to English.
intro.cn: precaution 是一个拉丁语复合词，意为「在事情之前完成的看守」，经法语传入英语。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, in place as well as in time, so it adds the idea of doing something ahead of the event.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前」，既指空间上的前面，也指时间上的先前，因此给词根加上「提前」的意思。

items.en: Cavere meant to be on guard, to take care or to watch out, and it also gave English caution and caveat.
items.cn: cavere 意为当心、提防、留意，英语的 caution 与 caveat 也来自它。

items.en: Joined together, prae- and cavere produced praecautio, a guarding done beforehand, with the noun ending -tio naming the action.
items.cn: prae- 与 cavere 合起来构成 praecautio，指「事先做的提防」，名词词尾 -tio 表示动作。

items.en: French took the Latin noun as précaution and passed it into English, where the accent was soon dropped from the spelling.
items.cn: 法语把这一拉丁名词写作 précaution 并传入英语，英语拼写随后去掉了重音符号。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for both the prior care and the concrete measures that carry it out, with the plural naming a set of safety arrangements.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它指事先的谨慎，也指落实这种谨慎的具体措施；复数则指一整套安全安排。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two Latin parts and the caution family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for protection taken in advance.
note.cn: 形近组沿两个拉丁构件与 caution 词族展开；近义组收其他表示「提前防护」的词。

entries.definition: Care taken to avoid danger; from the same Latin verb cavere.
entries.definitionCN: 避免危险的谨慎；与 precaution 同出拉丁动词 cavere。

entries.definition: Careful to avoid risk or danger.
entries.definitionCN: 小心避开风险或危险的；谨慎的。

entries.definition: A warning that something may not be true or may fail.
entries.definitionCN: 提醒某事可能不成立或会出问题的警告。

entries.definition: Acting as a protection against something that might happen.
entries.definitionCN: 起预防作用的；防备性的。

entries.definition: Something that protects people from harm or loss.
entries.definitionCN: 保护人们免受伤害或损失的东西；保障措施。

entries.definition: An action taken to deal with a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 为处理某个问题而采取的行动；措施。

entries.definition: The state of being kept safe from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 受到保护、免于伤害的状态。

entries.definition: Careful thinking about what will be needed later.
entries.definitionCN: 对日后需要的东西所做的预先考虑。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin parts, a prefix of before and a verb of watching, combine into one noun that always looks ahead.
normalIntro.cn: 两个拉丁构件，一个表示「在前」的前缀和一个表示「看守」的动词，合成一个总是朝前看的名字。

normal.en: Praecautio is literally a guarding before: prae- adds before, cavere adds the watching.
normal.cn: praecautio 字面就是「事先的看守」：prae- 加上「在前」，cavere 加上「看守」。

normal.en: Caution is the heart of the word and cautious is its adjective, so the family always points to care rather than to repair.
normal.cn: caution 是这个词的核心，cautious 是它的形容词，可见这个词族总是指向「小心」，而不是「事后修补」。

normal.en: Take precautions: the verb take shows that these are things you carry out, not feelings you have.
normal.cn: take precautions 里的 take 说明这些是可以执行的做法，而不是心里的感觉。

normal.en: As a precaution works like an adverbial phrase, naming the reason for an action rather than the action itself.
normal.cn: as a precaution 起状语短语的作用，说明做某事的理由，而不是那件事本身。

normal.en: Caveat comes from the same Latin verb and means let him beware, a warning rather than a measure.
normal.cn: caveat 出自同一个拉丁动词，意思是「让他当心」，是警告而不是措施。

abstract.en: A precaution is a bet paid in advance against a loss you hope never arrives.
abstract.cn: 预防措施是为一场你希望永不发生的损失提前付下的赌注。

abstract.en: The word puts care before the event, which is why it never describes a rescue.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「小心」放在事件之前，所以它从不描述救援。

abstract.en: Every precaution admits that something can go wrong, and does something about it anyway.
abstract.cn: 每一个预防措施都承认事情可能出错，却仍然为此做了点什么。

examples.en: Take precautions against fire before the dry season begins.
examples.cn: 旱季到来之前要采取防火措施。

examples.en: She copied the files as a precaution.
examples.cn: 她把文件复制了一份，以防万一。

examples.en: The factory's safety precautions were found to be inadequate.
examples.cn: 这家工厂的安全防范措施被认定不到位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞考神」——出门前先扑上去求考神保佑，就是预防；precaution 是预防措施。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前、预先）+ cavere（当心、提防）→ praecautio（事先的提防）→ 法语 précaution → 英语 precaution。

sensesIntro.en: The core is care placed before the event; the senses divide into the prior watchfulness, the single step that carries it out, and the organised set of such steps.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「放在事情之前的谨慎」；义项分出事先的警觉、落实警觉的单项做法，以及成套的这类做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands checking the door and the gas valve before leaving the house.
core.cn: 核心意象：出门前那双手把门窗和煤气阀逐一检查一遍。

branches.en: boards nailed over a shop window before a storm
branches.cn: 台风前钉在店窗上的木板

branches.en: a hand pausing to test whether the stove is off
branches.cn: 一只手停下来试炉子是否关好

branches.en: a printed list of fire rules on a factory wall
branches.cn: 工厂墙上印着的一列消防规定

branches.en: sandbags at the door and a checklist on the wall
branches.cn: 门口的沙袋与墙上的检查清单

branches.en: the quiet habit of looking twice before locking up
branches.cn: 锁门前习惯性多看一遍的安静举动

intro.en: Two Latin parts, a prefix of before and a verb of watching, combine into one noun; English then added a suffix for the adjective.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁构件，表示「在前」的前缀和表示「看守」的动词，合成一个名词；英语再为它加上构成形容词的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix and the verb, and the compound noun built from them; French carried that noun into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了前缀、动词以及由二者构成的复合名词；法语把这个名词带进了英语。

scene: 音乐能激发孩子的想象力。 Music can stimulate a child's imagination.

senses.definition: to make someone feel interested or eager to think
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生兴趣或乐于思考
senses.example: Music can stimulate a child's imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐能激发孩子的想象力。
senses.why: This is the mental sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是心智层面的义项。

senses.title: Make more active

senses.example: The plan is meant to stimulate the economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划旨在刺激经济。
senses.why: A spark makes a fire grow faster.
senses.whyCN: 火星让火烧得更旺。

senses.title: Excite the body

intro.cn: stimulate 来自拉丁语 stimulare（驱赶），源于 stimulus（赶牛用的尖刺棒）。

items.en: Stimulus named a goad or prick.
items.cn: stimulus 指刺棒或尖刺。

items.en: Stimulare meant to prick into action.
items.cn: stimulare 意为刺促使动。

items.en: Stimulate entered English as a learned verb.
items.cn: stimulate 作为学术动词进入英语。

items.en: It named the waking of body and mind.
items.cn: 它指唤醒身体与心智。

items.en: It spread to markets and growth.
items.cn: 它扩展到市场与增长。

note.en: Stimulate is compared with look-alike words and with words for arousing and encouraging.
note.cn: 把 stimulate 与形近词以及表示激发和促进的词作比较。

to state as a condition
a substance that makes you more active

normalIntro.en: Stimulate began as a goad that moved cattle and now moves minds and markets.
normalIntro.cn: stimulate 起初是赶牛的刺棒，如今又能推动头脑与市场。

normal.en: Good questions stimulate thought.

normal.en: Exercise stimulates blood flow.

abstract.en: A small goad moves a large animal.
abstract.cn: 一根小刺棒，能推动一头大牲口。

abstract.en: Interest grows where something first pricks it.

examples.en: Cold water stimulates the skin.
examples.cn: 冷水刺激皮肤。

dict_mnemonic.text: stimulate 来自拉丁语「赶牛刺棒」，所以是「刺激、激发」；stimulate interest 是激发兴趣，stimulate the economy 是刺激经济，名词是 stimulus。

root: 拉丁语 stimulus（赶牛刺棒）加动词词尾；由刺动牲口，引申为激发兴趣、刺激增长与唤起生理反应。

sensesIntro.en: Stimulate means to awake interest, to speed up growth, or to make a body respond.
sensesIntro.cn: stimulate 指唤醒兴趣、加快增长，或使身体产生反应。

core.en: A small point that starts movement.
core.cn: 一个启动运动的小尖点。

branches.en: A song opens a child's mind.
branches.cn: 一首歌打开了孩子的心智。

branches.en: A new road brings trade to a town.
branches.cn: 一条新路给小镇带来贸易。

intro.cn: stimulate 加动词词尾，其同族词包括 stimulus 与 stimulation。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base stimulus means a goad.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 stimulus 意为刺棒。

definition_zh: 粉末；粉状物；粉状用品；火药；扑粉；撒粉；搽粉
definition_en: a dry solid crushed into very small grains, a product sold in that form, an explosive, a cosmetic dust for the skin, or to put such dust on something
core_image: 石臼里一块干香料被杵子碾碎，细粉从臼沿滑落，堆成浅浅一小堆

senses.title: A solid crushed into fine grains
senses.definition: a dry solid substance broken into very small grains, like dust
senses.definitionCN: 干燥的固体被弄成极细的颗粒，状如灰尘
senses.example: The mortar had been ground to a fine powder.
senses.exampleCN: 研钵里的东西已经被磨成细粉。
senses.why: Latin pulvis meant dust, so the word starts from the state a hard thing reaches after it is crushed, not from any particular material.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pulvis 意为灰尘，所以这个词的起点是硬物被碾碎之后达到的状态，而不是某种特定的材料。

senses.title: A product sold in this form
senses.definition: a household or food product made and sold as fine grains, such as a washing or milk powder
senses.definitionCN: 以细颗粒形态制造并出售的家用或食品用品，如洗衣粉、奶粉
senses.example: She added a scoop of milk powder to the warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 她往温水里加了一勺奶粉。
senses.why: Once the form has a name, the goods packed in that form borrow it, so the word moves from a texture to a whole class of products.
senses.whyCN: 这种形态一旦有了名字，装成这种形态出售的商品就借用了它，于是词义从一种质地转到一整类产品。

senses.title: The explosive used in guns
senses.definition: an explosive mixture of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, used to fire guns and cannon
senses.definitionCN: 硝石、硫磺和木炭混合成的爆炸物，用来发射枪炮
senses.example: The old fort stored barrels of powder in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 旧要塞的地窖里存放着一桶桶火药。
senses.why: Gunpowder was the first powder that mattered in European daily life, so the bare word could stand for it alone; the compound gunpowder later made that clear.
senses.whyCN: 在欧洲日常生活中，火药是最早重要起来的一种粉，所以单说这个词就能指它；后来才用复合词 gunpowder 把这层意思说明白。

senses.title: Cosmetic dust for the skin
senses.definition: a fine cosmetic dust pressed or loose, used to make skin look smoother
senses.definitionCN: 细滑的化妆用粉，压成粉饼或散装，用来让皮肤看起来更匀净
senses.example: She patted powder onto her cheeks before the camera flashed.
senses.exampleCN: 闪光灯亮起前，她在脸颊上轻轻扑了粉。
senses.why: A face powder is simply the same material applied to skin, so the word narrows by context rather than by any new root.
senses.whyCN: 扑面粉不过是把同一种材料用到皮肤上，所以这一义项是靠语境收窄的，并没有换词根。

senses.title: To dust something with powder
senses.definition: to put powder on a surface or on the skin, usually in a thin layer
senses.definitionCN: 把粉薄薄地撒在某个表面或皮肤上
senses.example: He powdered the baby's skin before dressing her.
senses.exampleCN: 他给婴儿的皮肤扑了粉，再给她穿衣服。
senses.why: English often turns a mass noun into a verb without any ending, and to powder is exactly the act of applying the material the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把不可数名词直接当动词用，to powder 正是把名词所指的材料涂抹上去的动作。

intro.en: Powder is Latin dust filtered through French: pulvis became poudre, and English trimmed the spelling and widened the meaning.
intro.cn: powder 是拉丁语「灰尘」经法语滤过来的词：pulvis 变成 poudre，英语又简化了拼写并扩大了词义。

items.en: Pulvis meant dust or powder, and its stem pulver- carried the idea of something ground very fine.
items.cn: pulvis 意为灰尘、粉末，它的词干 pulver- 表示被磨得极细的东西。

items.en: The oblique form pulverem carried the word into popular Latin, and it is the shape behind the Romance words for dust.
items.cn: pulvis 的斜格形式 pulverem 把这个词带入通俗拉丁语，罗曼语族表示灰尘的词都从这一形式来。

items.en: Old French reduced the word to poudre, the everyday term for dust and for ground spices.
items.cn: 古法语把它简化成 poudre，是当时指灰尘与研磨香料粉的日常说法。

items.en: Middle English wrote it poudre or powder, first for dust and spices, then for the explosive that changed warfare.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 poudre 或 powder，先指灰尘和香料粉，后来也指改变战争方式的火药。

items.en: Modern English settled on powder and added washing powders, milk powders, face powder and the verb to powder.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为 powder，并添上洗衣粉、奶粉、扑面粉以及动词 to powder 等用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same Latin dust stem plus compounds; the near-meaning group gathers words for loose grains and fine material.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁「灰尘」词干上的形式与复合词；近义组收表示松散颗粒与细碎物质的词。

entries.definition: Like powder, or covered with a thin layer of fine dust.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powder 加 -y 构成，义为「粉状的；覆着细粉的」。

entries.definition: Made into powder or dusted with it, as in powdered sugar.
entries.definitionCN: 由 powder 加 -ed 构成，义为「制成粉的；撒了粉的」，如糖粉。

entries.definition: An explosive mixture of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal, built from gun and powder.
entries.definitionCN: 由 gun 与 powder 复合，指硝石、硫磺与木炭混成的火药。

entries.definition: To crush something into dust, from the Latin stem pulver- that also stands behind powder.
entries.definitionCN: 与 powder 同出拉丁词干 pulver-，义为「把……碾成粉」。

entries.definition: Fine dry particles of earth or other matter that settle on surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 灰尘；指落在地面或物体表面的细土与碎屑。

entries.definition: A single small hard particle of a substance such as sand or salt.
entries.definitionCN: 颗粒；指沙、盐等物质的一粒小硬粒。

entries.definition: A small grain, often one of many pressed together into a larger form.
entries.definitionCN: 小颗粒；常指压成较大形状的许多小粒之一。

entries.definition: Grain ground into a fine powder and used for baking.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉；指磨成细粉的谷物，专用于烘焙。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin dust in English clothes, and its family keeps returning to crushed solids, packed goods and the act of dusting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是穿上英语外衣的拉丁语「灰尘」，同族词反复回到碾碎的固体、包装出售的货品与撒粉的动作。

normal.en: Powder comes from Latin pulvis, dust, so the original idea is matter reduced to grains too small to hold.
normal.cn: powder 来自拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘），原意是被弄成小到抓不住的颗粒的物质。

normal.en: Old French kept the word as poudre, and English simply dropped the u in the spelling.
normal.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 poudre，英语只是把拼写里的 u 去掉了。

normal.en: Powdery adds -y and describes anything that looks or feels like powder.
normal.cn: powdery 加 -y，用来形容看起来或摸起来像粉的东西。

normal.en: Gunpowder is gun plus powder, which is why the bare word can still mean the explosive in older writing.
normal.cn: gunpowder 是 gun 加 powder，所以在较早的文字里单说 powder 仍可指火药。

normal.en: Washing powder and milk powder are named for their form, not for what they contain.
normal.cn: 洗衣粉与奶粉是按形态命名的，不是按成分命名的。

abstract.en: A solid loses its shape when it becomes powder, so the word sits halfway between a substance and its dust.
abstract.cn: 固体变成粉就失去了形状，所以这个词停在「物质」与「它的尘」之间。

abstract.en: The same dust can feed a baby, clean a shirt or blow down a wall, and English keeps one word for all three.
abstract.cn: 同一种粉可以喂婴儿、洗衣服或炸塌一堵墙，英语对这三件事只用一个词。

abstract.en: To powder a face is to add a layer thin enough to look like nothing at all.
abstract.cn: 给脸扑粉，是加上薄到看不出的一层。

examples.en: The mortar had been ground to a fine powder.
examples.cn: 研钵里的东西已经被磨成细粉。

examples.en: She added a scoop of milk powder to the warm water.
examples.cn: 她往温水里加了一勺奶粉。

examples.en: He powdered the baby's skin before dressing her.
examples.cn: 他给婴儿的皮肤扑了粉，再给她穿衣服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡得」——热水一冲，奶粉就泡得开；powder 就是粉末、粉状物。

root: 源自拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘、粉末），词干 pulver- 见于 pulverize；经古法语 poudre 进入英语，中古英语写作 poudre 或 powder，近代定型为 powder。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a solid crushed to dust; the senses spread to goods sold in that form, the explosive, cosmetic dust, and the act of putting it on.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被碾成细尘的固体；义项由此分出以这种形态出售的用品、火药、化妆用的粉，以及把粉扑上去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pestle grinding a dry spice in a stone bowl while fine dust slips over the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：石臼里一块干香料被杵子碾碎，细粉从臼沿滑落，堆成浅浅一小堆。

branches.en: a pestle grinding dry spice at the bottom of a stone bowl
branches.cn: 杵子在石臼底把干香料碾碎

branches.en: a scoop of milk powder tipped into warm water
branches.cn: 一勺奶粉倒进温水

branches.en: barrels of black powder stacked in a fort cellar
branches.cn: 要塞地窖里堆着的黑色火药桶

branches.en: a brush tapping powder onto a cheek
branches.cn: 刷子把粉轻轻拍上面颊

branches.en: a cook dusting flour over a rolling board
branches.cn: 厨师把面粉撒在案板上

intro.en: The word is Latin dust carried through French, with an English suffix that turns it into a description and a compound that turns it into an explosive.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「灰尘」经法语传来，再加一个英语后缀变成形容词，加一个复合成分变成火药。

latinIntro.en: Powder goes back to Latin pulvis, dust, whose stem pulver- also gives pulverize; the form reached English through Old French poudre.
latinIntro.cn: powder 上溯拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘），其词干 pulver- 也造出 pulverize；这个词形经古法语 poudre 进入英语。

definition_zh: 唤起；激起；唤醒；引起
definition_en: to cause a feeling or reaction to appear, or to wake someone
core_image: 轻轻一推，让沉睡的东西动起来
scene: 台下的人原本昏昏欲睡。 The speaker aroused their interest with a single question.
sceneCN: 这里 arouse 是「激起」（第 1 个义项：使某种情绪或反应产生）；句意是演讲者用一个问题激起了他们的兴趣。

derivatives.zh: 名词：唤起；激发
形容词：令人激动的

senses.title: To stir up a feeling
senses.definition: to make an emotion or reaction begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情绪或反应开始存在
senses.example: The speaker aroused their interest with a single question.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者用一个问题激起了他们的兴趣。
senses.why: Rouse meant to shake someone awake; arouse adds the idea of setting a feeling in motion.
senses.whyCN: rouse 意为把人摇醒；arouse 则添上「让某种情绪动起来」的意思。

senses.title: To wake someone
senses.definition: to bring a sleeping person back to waking
senses.definitionCN: 使睡着的人回到清醒状态
senses.example: The noise aroused him from a deep sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 那声响把他从沉睡中唤醒。
senses.why: This is the older physical sense, still used when the waking is gentle or slightly literary.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的身体义，在语气温和或略偏书面时仍在使用。

senses.title: To provoke a hostile reaction
senses.definition: to cause suspicion, anger, or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 引起怀疑、愤怒或批评
senses.example: His sudden wealth aroused suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的突然暴富引起了怀疑。
senses.why: Once the word could start any feeling, it naturally covered unpleasant ones such as doubt and anger.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能启动任何情绪，自然也涵盖怀疑、愤怒这类不快的情绪。

intro.en: Arouse is a- 'up' added to the older verb rouse.
intro.cn: arouse 是在更古的动词 rouse 前加上 a-「向上」构成的。

items.en: ruser meant 'to drive back, to startle'.
items.cn: ruser 意为「击退、惊起」。

items.en: English rouse meant 'to shake awake'.
items.cn: 英语 rouse 意为「摇醒」。

items.en: The prefix a- added the sense 'up, into motion'.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 增添了「向上、动起来」的意思。

items.en: Arouse appeared with the sense of waking or stirring.
items.cn: arouse 出现时意为唤醒或使动起来。

items.en: Feelings and suspicions became its commonest objects.
items.cn: 情绪与怀疑成了它最常见的宾语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the rouse stem; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of stirring feeling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 rouse 词干；近义组是其他激起情绪的词。

sensesIntro.cn: 叫醒睡着的人与点燃一种情绪，用的是同一种推力。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手轻轻推动沉睡的身体。

definition_zh: 有说服力的；能打动人心的；令人信服的
definition_en: able to make a person believe something or agree to act, or having the quality that wins people over
core_image: 一句话落到桌面，原本摇头的人把椅子向前挪了半寸
scene: 会议室里，一位年轻人只讲了三分钟，原本交抱双臂的经理们开始翻看方案。 Her persuasive summary turned a room of doubtful managers into supporters within three minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 persuasive 指「论证足以让人改变判断，并愿意跟着行动」（第 1 个义项：使人信服的力量）；句意为她那段有说服力的总结，让满屋子原本怀疑的经理在三分钟内变成了支持者。可辨识物件：投影仪、会议桌、摊开的方案、半杯咖啡；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有说服力的；能打动人的

senses.title: Convincing to the mind
senses.definition: of an argument or a case, strong enough to make a reasonable listener accept it
senses.definitionCN: 指论证或理由足够有力，使通情理的听者接受
senses.example: The report made a persuasive case for restoring the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为恢复那片沼泽提出了有力的理由。
senses.why: the adjective simply names the power that the verb describes: what can persuade is persuasive.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给动词所描述的那种力量命名：能说服人的，就是「有说服力的」。

senses.title: Effective in moving people to act
senses.titleCN: 能促使人真的行动起来
senses.definition: of a text or a campaign, able to produce action and not only agreement
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或活动不仅使人同意，还能促成实际行动
senses.example: A persuasive poster cut household water use by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 一张有说服力的海报让家庭用水减少了五分之一。
senses.why: persuading has always ended in an act in English, so the adjective inherits that push toward doing.
senses.whyCN: 英语里的 persuade 一向以「行动」收尾，因此这个形容词也继承了那股推向行动的力量。

senses.title: Skilled at winning others over
senses.titleCN: 指人善于把别人争取过来
senses.definition: of a person, habitually able to make others agree with him or her
senses.definitionCN: 指某人一贯能把别人说得同意自己
senses.example: She is the most persuasive member of the negotiating team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是谈判小组里最善于说服人的成员。
senses.why: the quality moves from the argument to the person who habitually produces such arguments.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质从「论证」移到了「惯常做出这种论证的人」身上。

senses.title: Winning in manner
senses.titleCN: 举止动人、令人乐于亲近
senses.definition: of a smile, voice or manner, pleasing in a way that makes people willing
senses.definitionCN: 指笑容、声音或举止讨人喜欢，使人愿意应允
senses.example: His persuasive smile opened doors that argument could not.
senses.exampleCN: 他那动人的笑容打开了论证打不开的门。
senses.why: the old link between the root and sweetness survives in this sense, where charm replaces reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 词根与「甜」的古老联系在这一义项里留存下来：魅力取代了论理。

senses.title: Apparently sound but unproven
senses.definition: of an explanation, plausible enough to be tempting although the evidence stops short of proof
senses.definitionCN: 指某种解释颇有道理、引人相信，但证据尚不足以证明
senses.example: The correlation is persuasive but far from conclusive.
senses.exampleCN: 这项相关性颇有说服力，却远未成为定论。
senses.why: English often marks the gap between sounding convincing and being true, and persuasive sits exactly on that line.
senses.whyCN: 英语常区分「听着可信」与「确实为真」，而 persuasive 正落在这条线上。

senses.title: Forceful and vivid in style
senses.definition: of writing or speech, carrying the reader along through force and clear images
senses.definitionCN: 指文章或言辞以力量与清晰的意象把读者带着走
senses.example: The essay is persuasive because every image is sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章有力，是因为每个意象都鲜明。
senses.why: style persuades by making the reader see, so the word came to describe craft as well as logic.
senses.whyCN: 文风靠让读者看见来说服，于是这个词也用来描述写作手艺，而不只描述逻辑。

senses.title: Strong enough to overcome doubt
senses.definition: of an answer or a reason, weighty enough to quiet a specific doubt
senses.definitionCN: 指回答或理由足够有分量，能压住具体的疑虑
senses.example: No persuasive answer came from the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 部里没有给出一个足以释疑的答复。
senses.why: this sense measures the adjective against a particular objection rather than against truth in general.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项衡量的是它能否压住某个具体反对意见，而不是一般意义上的真假。

senses.title: Enough to sway a jury
senses.definition: of evidence in law, sufficient to move a court or jury toward a finding
senses.definitionCN: 指法律上的证据足以使法院或陪审团倾向于某一认定
senses.example: The defence called the fingerprint match persuasive.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方称那处指纹吻合具有说服力。
senses.why: courts need a word for evidence that convinces without being conclusive, and this adjective fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要一个词来形容「足以令人信服但不必 conclusive」的证据，这个形容词正好补上这个位置。

intro.en: Persuasive is persuade plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus, which reached English through Old French -if. It names the quality of what can persuade.
intro.cn: persuasive 是 persuade 加上拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus，该词尾经古法语 -if 进入英语。它命名的是「能说服人」这种性质。

items.en: The root suadere 'to advise, urge' supplies the meaning; its link with suavis 'sweet' is generally thought to be real but is not provable from the words alone.
items.cn: 词根 suadere「劝告、敦促」提供词义；它与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是真实的，但仅凭这两个词无法证明。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere gave persuadere, 'to prevail upon', the verb behind the adjective.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 suadere 得出 persuadere「争取过来」，即这个形容词背后的动词。

items.en: The ending -ivus marked a quality or a tendency, as in actus and activus; English took it through the French form -if.
items.cn: 词尾 -ivus 表示性质或倾向，如 actus 与 activus；英语经法语形式 -if 接受它。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the late sixteenth century, first of speeches and arguments, later of persons.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪晚期见于英语，最初用于演说与论证，后来才用于人。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it spread to advertising, statistics and law, wherever a claim has to carry a listener along.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，它扩展到广告、统计与法律，凡是一个主张需要带动听者的地方都用得上。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries differ by a few years on the earliest citation, and no attested pre-Latin form of the root exists, so deeper shapes are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对最早书证的年代相差数年；该词根在拉丁语之前没有有书证的形式，更深的形式均为重构。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that look close on the page but come from three different Latin verbs; group two holds adjectives that also move a listener, each with a different strength.
note.cn: 第一组收纸面上形近、却出自三个不同拉丁动词的形容词；第二组收同样能推动听者、但力道不同的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin pervadere 'spread through', built on vadere 'to go'; it means spreading everywhere, with no connection to advising.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pervadere「蔓延穿过」，由 vadere「走」构成；意为遍布各处，与「劝告」无关。

entries.definition: From permittere 'let through', built on mittere 'to send'; it means allowing rather than convincing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 permittere「放行」，由 mittere「送」构成；意为容许，而非说服。

entries.definition: The mirror adjective, built on dis- plus suadere: tending to advise someone away from an act.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像形容词，由 dis- 加 suadere 构成：倾向于劝人不要做某事。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the resulting belief; it is the base from which the adjective is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 表示行为或由此形成的信念的名词；正是构成这个形容词的基础。

entries.definition: Able to remove doubt about a fact; it leans on evidence where persuasive leans on the effect on the hearer.
entries.definitionCN: 能消除对某事实的怀疑；偏重证据，而 persuasive 偏重对听者的作用。

entries.definition: So forceful that attention and assent are almost forced; stronger and less polite than persuasive.
entries.definitionCN: 强到几乎迫使注意与赞同；比 persuasive 更重，也更不容气。

entries.definition: Of an argument, tightly reasoned and hard to answer; it praises structure rather than charm.
entries.definitionCN: 指论证严密、难以反驳；赞的是结构，不是魅力。

entries.definition: Moving through beautiful or forceful language; eloquent speech may persuade, but the word describes the speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 以优美或有力的言辞打动人；动人的话固然可能说服人，但这个词描述的是「说得漂亮」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the verb plus the Latin quality ending -ive, so it means 'having the power to persuade'.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是动词加拉丁性质词尾 -ive，意为「具有说服的力量」。

normal.en: The family runs persuade, persuasion, persuasive, persuasively, persuasiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 persuade、persuasion、persuasive、persuasively、persuasiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep it next to speech and evidence: a persuasive speech, persuasive evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与言辞、证据放在一起：有感染力的演讲、令人信服的证据。

normal.en: The negative form is unpersuasive, used of weak cases and flat writing.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unpersuasive，用于薄弱的理由与平淡的文字。

normal.en: The reverse adjective is dissuasive, the mirror of this one.
normal.cn: 反向的形容词是 dissuasive，正好是本词的镜像。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that rests lightly on a door and the door gives way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻放在门上，门就顺势开了。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp placed where everyone in the room must walk toward it.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯放在全屋人都不得不朝它走的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut so exactly that the lock turns on the first try.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙削得极准，第一下就把锁转开了。

examples.en: A persuasive letter can change a landlord's mind faster than a threat.
examples.cn: 一封有说服力的信，比一句威胁更快让房东改变主意。

examples.en: The lawyer built a persuasive narrative out of three ordinary facts.
examples.cn: 律师用三件平常的事实搭出一个令人信服的叙述。

examples.en: Her voice was quiet but persuasive in the crowded hall.
examples.cn: 在拥挤的大厅里，她的声音不高，却很有说服力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「per（彻底）+ suas（劝）+ ive（性质）」——劝到底的那种劲 → 有说服力的

root: 拉丁 persuasivus = per-（彻底）+ suadere（劝告）+ -ivus（性质词尾）；suadere 与 suavis「甜的」的联系一般认为是同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses ask one question in different places: how much carrying power does this argument, person, smile, style or piece of evidence actually have?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同场合问同一个问题：这段论证、这个人、这个笑容、这种文风或这份证据，究竟有多少带动人的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence laid on a table that makes a doubtful listener lean forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句落在桌面的话，让心存怀疑的听者把身子往前倾。

branches.en: CASES AND ANSWERS: a case is weighed, and a specific doubt is measured against it.
branches.cn: 理由与答复：一边称量理由是否成立，一边衡量它能否压住具体疑虑。

branches.en: FROM AGREEMENT TO ACTION: a poster changes behaviour, and evidence moves a jury toward a finding.
branches.cn: 从同意到行动：海报改变行为，证据推动陪审团走向某一认定。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same power is located first in skill, then in charm of manner.
branches.cn: 人本身：同一种力量先落在「技巧」上，再落到举止的魅力上。

branches.en: THE UNPROVEN: what merely sounds sound sits on the line between plausible and proven.
branches.cn: 未经证实者：只是「听着有理」的东西，正停在「可信」与「已证」之间。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: clear images and force of phrasing persuade without a single formal argument.
branches.cn: 写作手艺：鲜明的意象与有力的措辞，不必有一个正式论证也能说服人。

intro.en: Persuasive is built from a Latin verb plus a Latin quality ending, and both parts recur across English.
intro.cn: persuasive 由一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁性质词尾构成，两部分在英语中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin suadere gives persuade and dissuade, while -ivus gives a large family of English adjectives such as active and effective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suadere 衍生 persuade 与 dissuade，而 -ivus 衍生出 active、effective 等一大批英语形容词。

items.example: The prefix marks advice carried to its end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「劝到终点」。

items.example: The root carries the advising idea.
The ending turns a verb into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成一种性质。

items.example: He spoke persuasively about the risk.
items.exampleCN: 他有力地谈到了这项风险。

items.example: The persuasiveness of her case won the vote.
items.exampleCN: 她理由的说服力赢下了表决。
那个借口听起来没有说服力。

items.example: The fine had a dissuasive effect.
items.exampleCN: 这笔罚款起了劝阻作用。

items.example: Persuasion failed and the vote was called.
items.exampleCN: 说服失败，于是付诸表决。

definition_zh: 干涉；妨碍；干扰
definition_en: to become involved in something in a way that is not wanted, or to disturb what is happening
core_image: 一只手伸进两台正在咬合的齿轮之间，把事情搅乱
scene: 两个人在谈事情，第三个人忽然插进来替其中一人作答。 Please do not interfere while the machine is being repaired.
sceneCN: 这里 interfere 是「干涉、妨碍」（第 1 个义项：以不受欢迎的方式介入），句意机器正在修理，请勿干扰。画面里的物件：齿轮、插话的第三人、修理工具。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ence 构成，义为「干涉；干扰」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「爱管闲事的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「干涉者」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不干涉」

senses.title: Meddle in others' affairs
senses.definition: to take part in something that is not your business, often with unwelcome results
senses.definitionCN: 参与本不归你管的事，常常带来不受欢迎的后果
senses.example: The neighbours interfered in the argument and made it worse.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们插手这场争吵，反而让它更糟。
senses.why: Latin ferire means to strike; interferire is to strike in between two things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ferire 意为「击打」，interferire 即「在两者之间打进去」。

senses.title: Disturb or hinder
senses.definition: to hinder or disturb a process, signal, or activity that was working well
senses.definitionCN: 妨碍或扰乱原本进行良好的过程、信号或活动
senses.example: Bright lights interfere with the sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 强光会干扰传感器。
senses.why: Radio engineers took the verb up because one wave can strike across another.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师采用了这个动词，因为一束波会横穿过另一束。

senses.title: Touch what is not yours
senses.definition: to touch or handle something that you should leave alone, especially in a harmful way
senses.definitionCN: 触碰或摆弄本该不动的某物，尤指造成损害
senses.example: Do not let anyone interfere with the wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 别让任何人动那套线路。
senses.why: The original physical sense survives where hands actually meddle with objects.
senses.whyCN: 在最原始的身体意义上，这个词指手真的去碰东西。

intro.en: Interfere combines inter- "between" with the Latin verb ferire "to strike".
intro.cn: interfere 把 inter-「在……之间」与拉丁语动词 ferire「击打」结合在一起。

items.en: Ferire "to strike" was common in Latin for blows and struck deals.
items.cn: ferire「击打」在拉丁语中常见于「打」与「成交」的说法。

items.en: Interferire was rare and meant to come between with a blow.
items.cn: interferire 很少见，意为「用一击插到中间」。

items.en: French s'entreférir carried the idea of clashing or hitting against.
items.cn: 法语 s'entreférir 带有相撞、对冲的意思。

items.en: English first used interfere of horses striking their hooves together.
items.cn: 英语早期用 interfere 形容马匹的蹄子相撞。

items.en: The sense shifted to getting in the way, then to meddling in other's affairs.
items.cn: 意义转向「挡路」，再转向「插手别人的事」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the striking root; the near-meaning group holds other words for getting in the way.
note.cn: 形近组共享「击打」词根；近义组收其他表示「妨碍」的词。

entries.definition: The noun for meddling or for unwanted signal noise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干涉」或「干扰噪声」。

entries.definition: To work out a conclusion from evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，由证据推出结论。

entries.definition: To bury a body in the ground.
To busy oneself with what is not one's business.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「瞎掺和」，专指管闲事。

entries.definition: To break the calm or order of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰」，打破平静或秩序。

entries.definition: To block a path or process physically.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻碍」，以物理方式挡住。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on ferire, the blow hidden in the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在词中间藏着的 ferire「击打」上。

normal.en: Inter plus ferire: strike in between, and the gears jam.
normal.cn: inter 加 ferire：在中间打一记，齿轮就卡住了。

normal.en: Interfere with a plan, interfere in a quarrel.
normal.cn: 打乱计划用 with，插手争吵用 in。

normal.en: Static interferes with the radio signal.
normal.cn: 静电干扰无线电信号。

normal.en: Good parents watch, but do not interfere.
normal.cn: 好的父母看着，但不插手。

normal.en: Two interfering neighbours can spoil a quiet street.
normal.cn: 两个爱插手的邻居能毁掉安静的街道。

abstract.en: Help offered unasked can turn into interference.
abstract.cn: 未被请求的帮助会变成干涉。

abstract.en: Every blow struck between two things leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 打在两物之间的每一击都会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Some things grow best when nobody interferes.
abstract.cn: 有些东西在无人插手下才长得好。

examples.en: Parents should not interfere in their grown children's careers.
examples.cn: 父母不应干涉成年子女的职业选择。

examples.en: The new building may interfere with television reception.
examples.cn: 新楼可能会干扰电视信号。

examples.en: Wind interfered with the firefighting planes all afternoon.
examples.cn: 大风整个下午都妨碍着消防飞机作业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特费尔」——网上特费劲，因为总有人来干扰

root: 拉丁语 ferire「击打」→ inter-「在……之间」+ ferire → interferire「打进去」→ 古法语 s'entreférir → 英语 interfere。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: meddling in others' business, disturbing a process, and handling what should be left alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：插手别人的事、妨碍某个过程，以及乱动不该动的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into interlocking gears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进正咬合的齿轮之间。

branches.en: THE THREE TALKERS: the third voice breaks into a private talk.
branches.cn: 三人谈话这条线：第三个声音闯入私下的谈话。

branches.en: THE SENSOR: another light blinds the signal.
branches.cn: 传感器这条线：另一束光把信号晃瞎。

branches.en: THE WIRING: idle hands spoil a careful job.
branches.cn: 线路这条线：闲手毁掉细致的活儿。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses bring harm from the wrong place.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都是从错误位置带来的损害。

branches.en: THE LINK: disturbing objects is one way of meddling.
branches.cn: 连接线：乱动东西就是插手的一种。

intro.en: Interfere = inter- "between" + fer- "strike" + -e, the Latin verb ending.
intro.cn: interfere = inter-「在……之间」+ fer-「击打」+ -e（拉丁动词词尾）。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferire and the rare interferire are recorded, if thinly attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferire 与少见的 interferire 有记载，尽管材料不多。
