definition_zh: 冲突；抵触；（颜色、日程）不协调；撞击声
definition_en: to fight or disagree strongly, to look wrong together or happen at the same time, or a loud noise of metal hitting metal
core_image: 两面金属盾牌在半空相撞，火星四溅
scene: 两个人站在走廊两头，谁也不肯让路。 Their views clash whenever the budget comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 clash 指「冲突；抵触」（第 1 个义项：意见或利益尖锐对立）；句意是每次谈到预算，他们的看法就冲突。

derivatives.zh: 相互冲突的；不搭的
文化冲突

senses.title: A fight or strong disagreement
senses.definition: a short fight or a sharp disagreement between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体之间的短暂打斗或尖锐分歧
senses.example: A clash broke out between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 两个群体之间爆发了冲突。
senses.why: The sound of weapons meeting became the name of the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 兵器相击的声音，变成了这场相遇本身的名称。

senses.title: A bad match in time or colour
senses.definition: to look wrong together, or to be fixed for the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起显得不协调，或与另一事排在同一时间
senses.example: My lecture clashes with the football final.
senses.exampleCN: 我的讲座和足球决赛撞时间了。
senses.why: Two things that cannot sit together are said to strike each other, like metal on metal.
senses.whyCN: 无法并存的两件事被说成互相撞击，就像金属碰金属。

senses.title: A loud metallic noise
senses.definition: a hard, ringing sound made when metal objects hit each other
senses.definitionCN: 金属物件相撞时发出的刺耳响声
senses.example: The clash of the gates echoed down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 铁门的撞击声在街上传开。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the word began as an imitation of that noise.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个词最初就是模仿那种响声。

intro.en: Clash began as an imitative word for the noise of metal or weapons meeting.
intro.cn: clash 最初是模仿金属或兵器相撞之声的拟声词。

items.en: The word imitated a hard ringing impact.
items.cn: 这个词模仿坚硬物体相击的响声。

items.en: Clash named the noise of swords and armour.
items.cn: clash 指刀剑与甲片相击的声音。

items.en: The noun widened to any short fight.
items.cn: 名词扩展到任何短促的打斗。

items.en: Writers used it for disagreements of opinion.
items.cn: 作家们用它表示意见分歧。

items.en: The word now also covers colours and timetables.
items.cn: 这个词如今也用于颜色与日程。

note.en: The look-alike group holds noisy words with a similar ending, while the meaning group names open disagreements.
note.cn: 形近组列出结尾相近的声响词，近义组列出公开的分歧。

entries.definition: a violent collision or a loud breaking noise
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈的碰撞或破碎巨响

entries.definition: to hold something firmly
the sound of liquid hitting a surface
a serious disagreement that lasts some time
entries.definitionCN: 持续一段时间的严重分歧

entries.definition: an accident in which two moving things hit
entries.definitionCN: 两个运动物体相撞的事故

entries.definition: an angry argument between people who know each other

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the metallic sound, the timetable sense and the colour sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用金属声响、日程义与颜色义。

normal.en: Clash sounds like two cymbals: one hard hit, then ringing.
normal.cn: clash 听起来像两面钹：硬碰一下，然后余响。

normal.en: The word began with weapons, so every clash keeps a little violence.
normal.cn: 这个词起于兵器，所以每个 clash 都带一点火药味。

normal.en: Two meetings can clash, and so can a green shirt and red trousers.
normal.cn: 两场会可以撞时间，绿衬衫和红裤子也可以不搭。

normal.en: Clash with is the usual pattern: clash with a plan, clash with a colour.
normal.cn: clash with 是常用搭配：与计划冲突、与颜色不搭。

normal.en: A clash is shorter than a conflict and louder than a quarrel.
normal.cn: clash 比 conflict 短促，比 quarrel 更响亮。

abstract.en: Picture two shields meeting in mid-air with a spray of sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象两面盾牌在半空相撞，火星四溅。

abstract.en: Picture two calendars with the same evening blocked out twice.
abstract.cn: 想象两本日历上同一个晚上被圈了两次。

abstract.en: Picture a green scarf laid on a red coat and quickly taken away.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿围巾放在红大衣上，又赶紧被拿走。

examples.en: A clash broke out between the two groups at the gate.
examples.cn: 两个群体在大门口爆发了冲突。

examples.en: My lecture clashes with the football final.
examples.cn: 我的讲座和足球决赛撞时间了。

examples.en: The clash of the gates echoed down the empty street.
examples.cn: 铁门的撞击声在空街上回荡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「磕」，ash 想成「灰」：磕出灰来，就是撞得很响的冲突。

root: 源自英语本族的拟声词，模仿金属相击的脆响，后由声音义引申为打斗、意见冲突与不协调。

sensesIntro.en: A metallic noise becomes a fight, then a disagreement, then any two things that cannot fit together.
sensesIntro.cn: 金属响声先变成打斗，再变成意见冲突，最后变成任何无法并存的两件事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two metal shields striking with a spray of sparks.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面金属盾牌相撞，火星四溅。

branches.en: The noise of weapons becomes the fight itself.
branches.cn: 兵器之声变成了打斗本身。

branches.en: Things that cannot share a space seem to strike each other.
branches.cn: 无法共存的事物仿佛在互相撞击。

branches.en: The original sound sense stays in the noun.
branches.cn: 最初的声音义仍保留在名词里。

branches.en: Both senses keep the hardness of metal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了金属的硬度感。

branches.en: A fight and a bad match share the idea of collision.
branches.cn: 打斗与不搭共享碰撞这一概念。

intro.en: The verb base adds -es, -ed and -ing, and forms one compound noun.
intro.cn: 这个动词词基接 -es、-ed、-ing，并构成一个复合名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base: clash is a native imitative word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语词基：clash 是英语本族的拟声词。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 他的班次和我的撞上了。

items.example: Their schedules were clashing all week.
items.exampleCN: 他们整个星期的日程都在撞。

items.meaning: a conflict between ways of life
items.example: The office felt a culture clash.
items.exampleCN: 这间办公室感受到了文化冲突。

items.example: The crash came after the clash.
The clatter of trays filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 托盘碰响的声音充满了大厅。

definition_zh: 第十；十分之一
definition_en: coming after nine others in order, or one part of ten equal parts
core_image: 十根手指里最后立起的那一根
scene: 跑道尽头标着十个刻度，最后那条线属于领先者。 He finished the race in tenth place.
sceneCN: 这里 tenth 是「第十」（第 1 个义项：序数）；句意：他赛跑得了第十名。

derivatives.zh: 第十（列举用，加副词后缀 -ly）
什一税（同源旧词，指缴纳的十分之一）

senses.title: Coming after nine others
senses.definition: position number ten in a series
senses.definitionCN: 序列中的第十位
senses.example: Their office is on the tenth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的办公室在第十层。
senses.why: The ordinal marks the last finger in a full count, the edge of one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 序数标记整手点数后的最后一根手指，位于一双手的边缘。

senses.title: One part of ten equal parts
senses.definition: one of ten equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体十等分后的一份
senses.example: Rent takes a tenth of his salary.
senses.exampleCN: 房租占他工资的十分之一。
senses.why: A rank turns into a slice: the tenth item and the tenth share share one word.
senses.whyCN: 位次转成切片：第十项与第十份共享一词。

intro.en: Tenth is the ordinal of ten, formed in Old English with the Germanic -tha ending.
intro.cn: tenth 是 ten 的序数形式，古英语用日耳曼后缀 -tha 构成。

items.en: Old English teogotha was the ordinal of ten.
items.cn: 古英语 teogotha 是「第十」。

items.en: The -tha suffix built ordinals across the Germanic family, like German zehnte.
items.cn: -tha 后缀在日耳曼语族普遍构成序数，如德语 zehnte。

items.en: The deeper root dekm, ten, is a reconstructed Indo-European form.
items.cn: 更深的词根 dekm「十」是重构的印欧形式。

items.en: Spelling simplified to tenth, matching the hard th sound.
items.cn: 拼写简化为 tenth，与清辅音 th 一致。

items.en: The fraction sense grew with decimal mathematics.
items.cn: 小数数学的发展催生了「十分之一」义。

note.en: Tenth is set beside its cardinal and other ordinals.
note.cn: 把 tenth 与基数词及其他序数词并列。

entries.definition: the number itself
a cloth shelter; spelled without th, unrelated in sound use
entries.definitionCN: 帐篷；拼写相近，与序数无关

entries.definition: firmly fixed; looks similar in some fonts
the ordinal before tenth
the ordinal after tenth
one of ten equal groups in statistics

normalIntro.en: Real links: ten plus th, the last finger, one slice of ten, and decile in statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ten 加 th、最后一根手指、十等分之一、统计学的 decile。

normal.en: Tenth is ten wearing a th hat.
normal.cn: tenth 是戴着 th 帽子的 ten。

normal.en: The tenth floor is above nine floors.
normal.cn: 第十层在九层之上。

normal.en: A tenth of the pizza is one slice of ten.
normal.cn: 披萨的十分之一是十块中的一块。

normal.en: In tenth place: the last runner with a full count behind.
normal.cn: in tenth place：数满一双手后的最后一位。

normal.en: Decile is the Latin cousin of the tenth slice.
normal.cn: decile 是「十分之一」的拉丁表亲。

abstract.en: Ordinals are numbers wearing name tags.
abstract.cn: 序数是戴着名牌的数字。

abstract.en: The last finger closes the count and opens the fraction.
abstract.cn: 最后一根手指闭合计数，也开启分数。

abstract.en: Rank and share are one word apart.
abstract.cn: 位次与份额只隔一个词。

examples.en: She sits in the tenth row of the hall.
examples.cn: 她坐在大厅第十排。

examples.en: Only a tenth of applicants passed the test.
examples.cn: 只有十分之一的申请者通过了考试。

examples.en: The tenth of October is his birthday.
examples.cn: 十月十日是他的生日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼死」——跑第十名累得疼死 → tenth 第十

root: 古英语 teogotha「第十」，ten 的序数形式，日耳曼序数后缀 -tha 构成；与拉丁 decimus（第十）同出印欧 dekm。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses only: the rank after nine, and the slice of ten.
sensesIntro.cn: 仅两个义项：九之后的位次，与十等分之一。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last of ten counted fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：十根被数手指的最后一根。

branches.en: A name tag on position ten.
branches.cn: 挂在第十位上的名牌。

branches.en: The whole cut into ten identical slices.
branches.cn: 整体被切成十等份。

branches.en: Rank above, share below, one form.
branches.cn: 上是位次，下是份额，同一词形。

branches.en: Percentages and decimals live here.
branches.cn: 百分比与小数住在这里。

branches.en: Floors, rows and dates all borrow it.
branches.cn: 楼层、排次与日期都借用它。

intro.en: Tenth belongs to the Germanic ordinal family built with -th.
intro.cn: tenth 属日耳曼序数词族，以 -th 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordinals used -imus, as in decimus, tenth; English borrowed only the fraction idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语序数用 -imus 构成，如 decimus「第十」；英语只借入了「十分之一」的概念。

items.meaning: in the tenth place of a list

definition_zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的
definition_en: doing well and growing strong, especially in economic terms; wealthy and successful
core_image: 码头上吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯一直亮到深夜
scene: 铁路修通以后，原本安静的村子盖起了砖房，集市从清晨一直热闹到天黑。 Within a decade the quiet village had become a prosperous trading town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperous 是「繁荣的、兴旺的」（第 1 个义项：经济上有活力）；句意为十年之内，那个安静的村子变成了繁荣的贸易城镇。

pos.zh: 繁荣的；兴旺的；富裕的；成功的

derivatives.zh: prosperous 把 -ous 换成 -ity，得到「繁荣」这一状态名词
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economically strong and growing
senses.definition: having a strong economy, with growing trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 经济强劲、贸易、收入与就业都在增长的
senses.example: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the noun's outward signs but attaches them to a place: a town is prosperous when its cranes, ships and wages all point the same way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了名词那套看得见的迹象，只是把它们贴到一个地方身上：吊塔、船只与工资都朝同一个方向走，这座城就是繁荣的。

senses.title: Making money; financially successful
senses.definition: doing well in business and earning a good income
senses.definitionCN: 生意做得顺、收入可观的
senses.example: She runs a prosperous little bakery near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近经营一家生意兴隆的小面包店。
senses.why: The suffix -ous turns the state into a quality, so the word can sit straight on a shop or a firm that keeps earning; growth is now read in takings rather than in the size of a region.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 把状态变成一种性质，于是这个词可以直接贴到一家持续赚钱的店铺或公司上；这时增长是从营业额里读出来的，而不是从地区规模里读出来的。

senses.title: Wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: rich enough to live comfortably, especially of a person or a family
senses.definitionCN: 钱财足以过得舒适，尤指人或家庭
senses.example: Their prosperous neighbours lent them the money for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们富裕的邻居借钱给他们修屋顶。
senses.why: Applied to people, the same quality shifts from output to comfort: what shows is not trade figures but a full table, warm rooms and the spare money that can be lent to a neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 用到人身上，同一种性质就从产出转向舒适：显出来的不是贸易数字，而是一桌饭菜、暖和的房间，以及能借给邻居的余钱。

senses.title: Successful and favourable; thriving
senses.definition: doing well or likely to do well; favourable, especially of a period or an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 走得顺或可望走顺的；有利的，尤指一段时间或一项事业
senses.example: The firm entered a prosperous season after the treaty was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订之后，这家公司进入了一段顺遂的时期。
senses.why: The oldest Latin layer meant favourable or lucky, and that colour returns when the word describes a period or a plan rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的拉丁义层是「顺遂的、吉利的」，当这个词形容一段时间或一个计划而不是一个地方时，那层意味就回来了。

intro.en: Prosperous is the Latin adjective prosperus, built on pro- 'forward' and spes 'hope', and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: prosperous 就是拉丁形容词 prosperus，由 pro-「向前」与 spes「希望」构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Spes was the noun for hope, and the image behind it is a hope set in front of the eyes.
items.cn: spes 是表示希望的名词，背后的画面是把希望摆在眼前。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes formed prosperus, meaning favourable or fortunate; this is the usual analysis, though the details are debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 构成 prosperus，意为顺遂的、吉利的；这是通常的分析，细节仍有争议。

items.en: The verb prosperare meant to thrive or to make something thrive, and it fed both the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 动词 prosperare 意为兴旺、使兴旺，同时供养了形容词与名词。

items.en: Old French used prospere for fortunate and successful, and Middle English borrowed it in that shape.
items.cn: 古法语用 prospere 表示顺遂、成功，中古英语以这个形态借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperous describes economies, businesses, families and favourable periods, keeping the -ous adjective beside the -ity noun.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperous 可形容经济、企业、家庭与顺遂的时期，并让 -ous 结尾的形容词与 -ity 结尾的名词并排存在。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spes family and one near-spelling; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for wealth and healthy growth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spes 词族，并收一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示富裕与健康增长的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of doing well, formed with -ity where the adjective has -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，形容词用 -ous 结尾，名词用 -ity 结尾。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed and grow strong.
The adverb formed by adding -ly to this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -ly 构成的副词，意为兴旺地。

entries.definition: Only the spelling is close; this word means false and comes from Latin spurius, so the two are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，这个词意为虚假的，来自拉丁语 spurius，两者并无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: Growing strongly and doing well.
Having a lot of money and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与财物的。

entries.definition: Developing well and spreading strongly, often of plants, arts or business.
entries.definitionCN: 发展得好、势头旺盛的，常用于植物、艺术或生意。

entries.definition: Growing very fast, especially of trade or prices.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速增长的，尤指贸易或价格。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin adjective prosperus in English dress: pro- 'forward', spes 'hope', and the suffix -ous that makes a quality out of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是换上英语外衣的拉丁形容词 prosperus：pro-「向前」、spes「希望」，以及把二者变成性质的 -ous。

normal.en: Pro- is forward, spes is hope, and -ous turns the pair into a quality, so prosperous describes something that hope has favoured.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，-ous 把这一对变成性质，所以 prosperous 形容被希望照顾到的事物。

normal.en: The noun twin is prosperity: -ous marks the adjective, -ity marks the noun, and the stem never changes.
normal.cn: 名词搭档是 prosperity：-ous 标记形容词，-ity 标记名词，词干始终不变。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb in the middle: prosperity and prosperous are both built on it, one as a state and one as a quality.
normal.cn: 中间的动词是 prosper：prosperity 与 prosperous 都建在它上面，一个表状态，一个表性质。

normal.en: Desperate shares the Latin hope word spes but adds de- 'without', so the two words pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: desperate 共享拉丁语的希望 spes，但加上 de-「没有」，所以这两个词的方向正好相反。

normal.en: Note the spelling: the ending is -ous, not -ious, so there is no extra i before the u.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：结尾是 -ous 而不是 -ious，u 前面并没有多余的 i。

abstract.en: Think of a street where every second shutter is open and the lamps stay on late: that is prosperity seen as a quality.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，隔一家店就开着门，灯亮到很晚：这就是被看成一种性质的繁荣。

abstract.en: Add -ous and the word points at a thing; add -ity and it points at a condition. The suffix decides the grammar, not the meaning.
abstract.cn: 加 -ous，词就指向事物；加 -ity，词就指向状态。后缀决定语法角色，不决定意思。

abstract.en: A prosperous year and a year of prosperity say the same thing, one as a label and one as a period you can count.
abstract.cn: 「繁荣的一年」与「一段繁荣」说的是同一件事，一个像标签，一个像可以数出来的时间段。

examples.en: The city grew prosperous on shipping and insurance.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠航运与保险业繁荣起来。

examples.en: A prosperous town needs more than one good year.
examples.cn: 一座繁荣的城镇需要的远不止一个丰收年。

examples.en: They moved to a prosperous suburb with better schools.
examples.cn: 他们搬到了一个学校更好的富裕郊区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普罗斯珀勒斯」：先铺路，再拾珀，最后把家业勒紧攒起来，日子就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其动词 prosperare 意为兴旺；形容词经古法语 prospere 进入英语。一般认为词源分析成立，构词细节仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses keep the same picture of things going well; they differ only in where the success is read: a place, a business, a household, or a stretch of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项保留同一幅「事情顺利」的画面，区别只在于从哪里读出成功：一个地方、一门生意、一户人家，或一段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes turning over a busy dock while shop lights stay on late.
core.cn: 核心意象：繁忙码头上的吊塔不停转动，街边店铺的灯亮到深夜。

branches.en: a skyline of cranes above a working port
branches.cn: 工作港口上空的吊塔群

branches.en: a shop with a queue at the counter
branches.cn: 柜台前排着队的店铺

branches.en: a family eating in a warm dining room
branches.cn: 一家人在暖和的餐厅里吃饭

branches.en: a plan that keeps working out
branches.cn: 一步步走通的计划

branches.en: a town that stays lucky for years
branches.cn: 连续多年走运的城镇

intro.en: The stem is Latin; the two endings -ous and -ity do the English work of splitting quality from state.
intro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语；-ous 与 -ity 这两个结尾在英语里分工，一个表性质，一个表状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin recorded spes for hope, prosperus for fortunate, and prosperare for making something thrive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语留下了 spes（希望）、prosperus（顺遂的）与 prosperare（使兴旺）这几个形式。

items.exampleCN: 这门生意开始兴旺起来。

items.meaning: full of, having the nature of

definition_zh: 压碎；压坏；击溃；拥挤的人群
definition_en: to press something so hard that it breaks, or to defeat, or a crowd pressed tight
core_image: 一只脚踩在空罐上，罐身瞬间塌下去
scene: 他抬脚把空罐踩扁，铁皮发出脆响。 The machine will crush the stones into fine sand.
sceneCN: 这里 crush 指「压碎」（第 1 个义项：用大力把东西压破压扁）；句意是机器会把石头压成细沙。

derivatives.zh: 毁灭性的；压倒的
压碎机；碎石机
可压碎的

senses.title: Press until it breaks
senses.definition: to press something hard until it breaks or loses shape
senses.definitionCN: 用力压某物直到破裂或变形
senses.example: She crushed the garlic with the flat of a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 她用刀面把蒜压碎。
senses.why: Weight plus a hard surface ends a shape.
senses.whyCN: 重量加上硬面，就终结了一个形状。

senses.title: Defeat completely
senses.definition: to beat an opponent completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底打败对手
senses.example: The home team crushed the visitors by five goals.
senses.exampleCN: 主队以五球大胜客队。
senses.why: What is pressed flat cannot stand up again.
senses.whyCN: 被压平的东西，站不起来了。

senses.title: A tight crowd
senses.definition: a crowd pressed so tightly that movement is hard
senses.definitionCN: 挤得难以移动的人群
senses.example: We were caught in a crush at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们被堵在门口的拥挤人群里。
senses.why: Bodies packed like seeds in one pod.
senses.whyCN: 身体挤在一起，像豆荚里的豆子。

intro.en: Crush comes from Old French cruissir, to crack or gnash, perhaps from a Frankish word for pressing.
intro.cn: crush 源自古法语 cruissir（使裂开、咬牙），可能出自表示挤压的法兰克语词。

items.en: Cruissir meant to crack or to gnash the teeth.
items.cn: cruissir 意为使裂开或咬牙。

items.en: Crush first meant to break something by pressing.
items.cn: crush 最初指用挤压把东西弄破。

items.en: It was used for armies that broke an enemy.
items.cn: 它被用于形容军队击溃敌人。

items.en: A crowd pressed tight was called a crush.
items.cn: 挤得紧紧的人群被称为 crush。

items.en: It also names a strong but passing liking.
items.cn: 它也表示一种强烈却短暂的喜欢。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cr- opening and a hissing end, and the meaning group names other kinds of pressing and breaking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cr- 开头与嘶声结尾，近义组列出其他挤压与破坏的说法。

entries.definition: the hard outer layer of bread
a tool with stiff hairs
a loud fall or collision
to press something flat
to break into pieces with force
to beat someone in a contest

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a can under a foot and end with a team that cannot stand up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只被踩在脚下的罐子开始，落到一支站不起来的队伍。

normal.en: A foot and a can explain the whole word.
normal.cn: 一只脚和一只罐子，就解释了整个词。

normal.en: Press until the shape gives up.
normal.cn: 一直压，直到形状认输。

normal.en: A crushed team leaves the field flat.
normal.cn: 被击溃的队伍像被压平一样离场。

normal.en: In a crush, elbows do the talking.
normal.cn: 在拥挤的人群里，胳膊肘在说话。

normal.en: A crush is a feeling pressed into a small space.
normal.cn: 迷恋是被压进小小空间里的一份感情。

abstract.en: Picture a can folding under a boot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只罐子在靴子下折下去。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so tight that no one can turn.
abstract.cn: 想象人群紧得谁也没法转身。

abstract.en: Picture a paper cup flattened on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸杯被压扁在桌上。

examples.en: Do not crush the box; it holds glass.
examples.cn: 别把箱子压坏，里面有玻璃。

examples.en: The team crushed its rival in the final.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在决赛中击溃了对手。

examples.en: She was caught in the crush at the door.
examples.cn: 她被堵在门口的拥挤人群里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crush 记成「压到出声」：cr 像裂开的声响，ush 像一口气被挤出来。

root: 源自古法语 cruissir（使裂开、咬牙），可能出自表示挤压的法兰克语词；本义是压到破裂，后引申为击溃与挤紧的人群。

sensesIntro.en: From pressing a thing until it breaks, to breaking an enemy, to a crowd pressed tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西压破，到击溃对手，再到挤紧的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boot coming down on an empty can.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只靴子踩在一只空罐上。

branches.en: Pressing hard enough ends the shape of a thing.
branches.cn: 压得够狠，东西的形状就没了。

branches.en: A beaten team is a shape pressed flat.
branches.cn: 被打败的队伍，就是被压平的形状。

branches.en: A crowd can press bodies as a hand presses a can.
branches.cn: 人群挤身体，就像手挤罐子。

branches.en: The same force breaks metal and breaks a rival.
branches.cn: 同一种力既弄坏金属，也弄垮对手。

branches.en: Defeat and crowding both leave no room to move.
branches.cn: 失败与拥挤都让人没有转身的空间。

intro.en: Crush gathers words for pressing, breaking, and the machines that do it.
intro.cn: crush 这一族词围绕压、破，以及做这些事的机器。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word comes from Old French cruissir, to crack.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；这个词来自古法语 cruissir（使裂开）。

items.example: The news was a crushing blow.
items.exampleCN: 这消息是毁灭性的打击。

items.example: The box is crushable and light.

items.exampleCN: 他直白得让人招架不住。

items.meaning: a fence that holds back a crowd
items.example: Police stood at the crush barrier.
The worker had a crush injury.

definition_zh: 共和主义者；共和国的；共和党的
definition_en: a person who supports government by elected representatives, or something relating to a republic
core_image: 胸前别着一枚没有王冠的徽章，主张权力来自公民
scene: 集会上，一位共和主义者举着标语，主张废除君主、由选举产生元首。 The republican argued for an elected head of state.
sceneCN: 这里 republican 是「共和主义者」（第 1 个义项：支持共和政体的人）；句意：这位共和主义者主张由选举产生国家元首。

derivatives.zh: 共和国
共和主义

senses.title: A supporter of republican government
senses.definition: a person who believes that a country should be governed by elected representatives rather than a king
senses.definitionCN: 主张国家应由民选代表而不是国王治理的人
senses.example: The republican spoke against the power of the crown.
senses.exampleCN: 这位共和主义者发言反对王权。
senses.why: The ending -an marks a person connected with a republic, so the basic sense is the supporter of that system.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -an 标记与共和国相关的人，所以基本义是这种制度的支持者。

senses.title: Relating to a republic
senses.definition: describing something connected with a republic or its principles
senses.definitionCN: 描述与共和国或其原则相关的事物
senses.example: The country adopted a republican constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过了共和国宪法。
senses.why: The same -an ending also forms an adjective, which simply describes what belongs to a republic.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -an 词尾也能构成形容词，直接描述属于共和国的事物。

senses.title: A member of a republican party
senses.definition: a member or supporter of a political party that calls itself Republican
senses.definitionCN: 某个自称共和党的政党的成员或支持者
senses.example: The Republican won the state by a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 这名共和党人以微弱优势赢下了该州。
senses.why: Political parties borrow the word for their names, so the adjective becomes a party label.
senses.whyCN: 政党借用这个词作为名称，于是形容词又变成党派标签。

intro.en: Republican is republic plus the ending -an, which marks a person or an adjective connected with the base word.
intro.cn: republican 是 republic 加词尾 -an，表示与基础词相关的人或形容词。

items.en: The base is res publica, the public thing, a phrase for the shared state.
items.cn: 基础是 res publica（公共之事），指共享的国家。

items.en: Old French republique turns the phrase into the noun republic.
items.cn: 古法语 republique 把这一短语变成名词 republic。

items.en: Middle English republic names a state without a monarch.
items.cn: 中古英语 republic 指不设君主的国家。

items.en: Republican appears for a supporter of that form of government.
items.cn: republican 出现，指这种政体的支持者。

items.en: American and French politics turn the word into a party label.
items.cn: 美国和法国政治把这个词变成党派标签。

items.en: Modern English uses republican for both the believer and the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语中，republican 既指信奉者，也作形容词。

note.en: Republican is the person-and-adjective member of the republic family, and it sits near words for democratic and constitutional politics.
note.cn: republican 是 republic 词族中表示人或形容词的成员，与民主、宪政政治词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a state governed by elected representatives
belief in republican government
a supporter of government by the people
a person who supports government limited by a constitution
a person opposed to rule by a king or queen

normalIntro.en: Republican is republic plus -an, so the ending tells you it is either a person of that belief or an adjective of that system.
normalIntro.cn: republican 是 republic 加 -an，词尾告诉你它要么指持这种信念的人，要么是这种制度的形容词。

normal.en: Republic plus -an: a person who stands for the public thing.
normal.cn: republic 加 -an：为公共之事站台的人。

normal.en: The capital R version is a party name in American politics.
normal.cn: 大写 R 的版本是美国政治中的党派名称。

normal.en: Republican government is government without a monarch.
normal.cn: republican government 就是不设君主的政府。

normal.en: Compare republic and republicanism: the country and the belief.
normal.cn: 对比 republic 与 republicanism：国家与信念。

normal.en: The ending -an works like the -an in American, naming a person or an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -an 就像 American 中的 -an，表示人或形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a badge with no crown on it, worn on a plain jacket.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚没有王冠的徽章，别在朴素的夹克上。

abstract.en: Imagine a speaker at a rally pointing at a written constitution.
abstract.cn: 想象集会上的演讲者指着成文宪法。

abstract.en: Think of a ballot box standing where a throne used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象投票箱立在原来放王座的地方。

examples.en: The republican rejected the idea of a hereditary ruler.
examples.cn: 这位共和主义者拒绝世袭统治者的观念。

examples.en: The country wrote a republican constitution after the war.
examples.cn: 战后这个国家制定了共和国宪法。

examples.en: The Republican candidate visited three states in one day.
examples.cn: 这名共和党候选人一天走访了三个州。

dict_mnemonic.text: republic（共和国）+ -an（人／形容词词尾）＝共和主义者或共和国的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: republic（共和国，源自拉丁语 res publica「公共之事」）+ 词尾 -an，表示与共和国相关的人或性质。

sensesIntro.en: The believer comes first, then the adjective for the system, then the party member who borrows the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 先信奉这种制度的人，再是描述制度的形容词，最后是借用这个名称的政党成员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a citizen loyal to the public thing rather than to a crown.
core.cn: 核心意象：忠于公共之事、而非王冠的公民。

branches.en: The supporter of elected government is the central personal sense.
branches.cn: 支持民选政府的人，是核心的「人」的义项。

branches.en: The adjective describes whatever belongs to a republic.
branches.cn: 形容词描述属于共和国的一切。

branches.en: A party member carries the name into electoral politics.
branches.cn: 政党成员把这个名称带入选举政治。

branches.en: The believer and the adjective share the same loyalty to a republic.
branches.cn: 信奉者与形容词共享对共和国的忠诚。

branches.en: The system adjective becomes a party label through political use.
branches.cn: 制度形容词经政治使用变成党派标签。

intro.en: Republican is a transparent English formation from republic plus the ending -an.
intro.cn: republican 是 republic 加词尾 -an 构成的、构词透明的英语词。

latinIntro.en: The base republic goes back to res publica, the public thing, and -an marks a person or adjective connected with it.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 republic 可上溯到 res publica（公共之事），-an 标记与之相关的人或形容词。

items.example: Republic is the base of republican.
items.exampleCN: republic 是 republican 的基础词。

items.meaning: relating to or a person of

items.exampleCN: republican 由 republic 与 -an 合成。

items.example: Res publica is the distant source of republic.
items.exampleCN: res publica 是 republic 的远源。

items.example: Publica is the adjective inside res publica.
items.exampleCN: publica 是 res publica 中的形容词。
